FAILED' with an actual case-sensitive category split {'Food':1.00,'food':2.00} vs expected {'Food':3.00}. The frozen two-test recognizer confound does not explain these away.

The frozen two-test recognizer is a real grading defect observed directly: claude-expense-audit-v2 turn-00 hidden output is 'Ran 3 tests in 0.009s OK' yet the archived native record reports final_passed=false. That case was also independently rejected on one-turn/240.257s and no terminal event, so it is not promotable, but its full expense-contract correctness was never graded and remains unverified rather than proven bad.

Parent replay is final-code replay only, not per-turn file reconstruction. stress/balanced_review_v2.py regenerates each stage's public/hidden/parent-seed test definitions and runs them against the single final workspace/task.py; it never reconstructs the file state at each turn. A session that wrote a broken intermediate implementation and later corrected it would still be recorded as passing every stage. Per-turn artifact reconstruction is therefore an unverified property of all nine cases, including the three qualified ones.

Archive captures are first-stage excerpts only, not full provider-wire payloads (stated in the plan and TECH_DEBT); omission is proven for the captured excerpt stage, not for the entire wire. The hidden and parent seeds are regenerated by the same workload generator code the reviewer can read, so 'hidden' here means unseen by the model, not independent of the workload author.
